notes: Six documents: two university CTI pages (committee report, AI & academic integrity) and four College of Engineering pages; both coders set stance delegates on all six. The earlier agreement file for Cornell covered only two documents and has been replaced. Alignment was by source position of the anchors; the automatic pass mis-paired two units, which were re-paired by hand against the text (the FERPA/HIPAA privacy rule sentence, and the 'explanatory capacity' / 'data analysis' split). Pairs where one coder merged two rules into one unit (committee: instructor question banks plus the duty to validate them; engineering guidance: the student-use survey plus 'students are using it with or without our permission') were resolved by keeping both rules as two units, so the final file has 203 units (146 matched pairs, 45 only-A, 10 only-B kept, plus those 2 split-out units). Main disagreements: (1) policy_type for the three-option framework and tier sentences (P04 vs P05 vs P24/P42/P01), resolved by what the sentence says: who decides is P04, the named options are P05 once, each option carries its content (prohibit-where-foundational P42, allow-with-attribution P24, encourage P02); (2) teach-students-to-validate sentences addressed to instructors (P66 vs P31), resolved P31 by content with the duty in fit_note; (3) accessibility versus accommodation (P97 vs P51), resolved P51 when the passage is about accommodations under in-person assessment and not AI tool accessibility; (4) phase for duty and communication statements (course-start vs before-course vs general), resolved by what the sentence does (communicating expectations is course-start, design steps before-course, statements of institutional or faculty duty general, grading of student work during-assessment); (5) modality may/should/must on recommendation lists, resolved by the text's own verb ('should have', 'recommended steps' = should, 'Consider ...' / list options = may); (6) unit_stance permit/prohibit vs neutral for attribution and communication duties (neutral), restrict vs prohibit for upload limits (restrict); (7) actor student vs instructor vs all, resolved by who the sentence binds (imperatives to instructors = instructor, general statements = all); (8) P102/P63, P09/P49, P35/P60, P42/P43 type splits resolved by content. UNCOVERED: A's 'overreliance erodes interaction' and 'do not ignore student use' kept UNCOVERED; A's P54 for the Code-of-Academic-Integrity update recommendation was re-coded UNCOVERED. Only-A units (45): all kept as real statements (including list items of common uses and evidence examples). Only-B units (11): 10 kept, 1 dropped (a repeat of the 'consult the instructor' sentence in a second sample statement; coder A coded it once). new_types empty on both sides. Shares are over matched pairs using the coders' raw codes before resolution.
